simple.meaning: נִשְׁתְּוָן (nishtᵉvân) is a Hebrew word meaning “letter.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: נִשְׁתְּוָן (H5407) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 4:18, with occurrences in Ezra.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נִשְׁתְּוָן (H5407) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in נִשְׁתְּוָן (H5407) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: נִשְׁתְּוָן (nishtᵉvân) / H5407 is traced through Ezra 4:18, Ezra 4:23, Ezra 5:5 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: The letter which you sent to us has been plainly read before me.

timeline.evidenceText: The letter which you sent to us has been plainly read before me.
Then when the copy of king Artaxerxes’ letter was read before Rehum, Shimshai the scribe, and their companions, they went in haste to Jerusalem to the Jews, and made them to cease by force of arms.
But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they didn’t make them cease, until the matter should come to Darius, and an answer should be returned by letter concerning it.
